major_findings.title: Native host for the two Claude slots is pre-committed without disclosing the observed alternative host listing
major_findings.evidence: Amendment lines 113 and 127 assert `"native_host": "Claude"` for C-OPUS55 and C-SONNET55. But bound source summary.json (antigravity block) records `opus_5_5_selectors: [claude-opus-5-5-low, -medium, -high]` and `sonnet_5_5_selectors: [claude-sonnet-5-5-low, -medium, -high]`, and antigravity-catalog.json independently lists all six selectors with display names `Claude Opus 5.5 (Low/Medium/High)` and `Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Low/Medium/High)`. The original roster left this open: pre-run-decision-proposal-v1.json lines 118 and 145 both hold `"native_executable_or_transport": null` for `opus 5` and `sonnect 5`.
major_findings.why_this_matters: Line 190 scopes all claims to `explicitly approved native-stack comparisons only`, which makes the host part of the compared unit, not an implementation detail. The same nominal model family is observable on two hosts, and on Antigravity it carries an explicit effort tier that the Claude alias does not. Pinning one host silently introduces a design degree of freedom into an artifact whose declared purpose is to enumerate open decisions. Line 229 then reads `Exact Claude selection and identity/fallback capture`, which already presupposes the host rather than leaving it open.
major_findings.fix: Add to both C-OPUS55 and C-SONNET55: `alternative_host_listing_observed: ["claude-opus-5-5-low|medium|high"]` (and the sonnet equivalent) with `source_receipt` pointing at antigravity-catalog.json, plus `native_host_selection_status: "PROPOSAL_REQUIRES_USER_DECISION"`. Amend line 229 to read `Host assignment (Claude alias versus Antigravity effort-tiered selector) and exact Claude selection and identity/fallback capture`.
major_findings.realist_check: Realistic worst case is a host-confounded panel frozen without review of the alternative; contained in reporting by the line 190 native-stack disclaimer and detectable at selector-binding time. Nothing frozen, no spend, no data. Correctly MAJOR, not CRITICAL.

major_findings.title: Reasoning-effort omitted for both Codex slots, and the GPT-5.6 variant asymmetry is undisclosed inside the question being asked of the user
major_findings.confidence: HIGH on the catalog facts (read directly from bound source); MEDIUM on residual severity after the line 228 mitigation
major_findings.evidence: codex-catalog.json exposes `supported_reasoning_efforts` per model. gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.6-terra each support six levels (low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra). gpt-5.6-luna supports only five — it has no `ultra`. The amendment's REF-SOL61 slot (lines 77-87) and C-GPT56 slot (lines 88-107) carry no effort field at all, while C-FLASH38 carries three dedicated effort fields (lines 147-149). Line 102 presents `alternative_all_three: true` and lines 236-241 put a binary one-versus-three question to the user. Grep across pre-run-decision-proposal-v1.json, endpoint-amendment-v1.json and approval.json returns no match for effort/reasoning/xhigh/ultra — this amendment is the first artifact to encounter the dimension, so the omission is newly introduced, not inherited.
major_findings.why_this_matters: Two distinct consequences. First, the reference arm is `requires_new_matched_episodes: true` on a `budget_bounded_goal_completion_rate` endpoint, yet effort — which drives both completion and budget consumption — is not listed as a matching dimension, leaving `fresh matched` undefined on a load-bearing axis. Second, the user is being asked to choose `all three` without being told the three are not effort-symmetric: any effort policy that fixes or matches at `ultra` is unsatisfiable for gpt-5.6-luna. That is a latent infeasibility inside the option currently on the table. The amendment demonstrably recognises effort as a design variable — it built three fields for it on the Gemini slot — so the omission is asymmetric rather than uniform.
major_findings.fix: (1) Add `supported_reasoning_efforts_observed` and `selected_effort: null` to REF-SOL61 and C-GPT56, sourced to codex-catalog.json. (2) Add to C-GPT56.selection_proposal an explicit note: `variant_effort_support_is_not_symmetric: gpt-5.6-luna does not list ultra; gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.6-terra do`. (3) Add `effort` to the reference matching dimensions alongside `requires_new_matched_episodes`. (4) Surface the asymmetry in next_interview so the one-versus-three choice is made on complete information.
major_findings.partial_mitigation_acknowledged: Line 228 does list `provider-specific effort/context policy` as a remaining blocking decision, which generically covers Codex effort. That mitigation does not cover the undisclosed Luna/ultra asymmetry, the missing per-slot effort records that a future freeze would bind to, or the reference matching gap.
major_findings.realist_check: Realistic worst case is a re-amendment after a user picks `all three` and the effort policy proves unsatisfiable for Luna, or arms running at unstated/unequal effort corrupting the budget-bounded primary. Mitigated by line 228, by the absence of any freeze, and by binding-time detection for Luna; the reference-matching gap is the element most likely to survive undetected. Correctly MAJOR, not CRITICAL — no data, no spend, no freeze.

shared_unverified_fields (lines 65-75) holds one global block for entitlement, served identity, parity and cost. All values are currently null/false so nothing is misstated today, but the schema cannot express a partially-verified roster — the first slot to acquire a receipt will have no place to record it without either mutating the shared block or silently implying the state applies to all slots.

Each slot expresses 'not yet selected' differently: `selected_for_assignment: false` (REF-SOL61), `selected_variants: null` (C-GPT56), `replacement_adopted: false` (C-OPUS55/C-SONNET55), `selected_effort_selector: null` (C-FLASH38). Semantically correct everywhere; mechanically awkward for any downstream completeness check over the roster.

multi_perspective_notes.executor: With this draft alone an executor could not bind a single selector: both Claude slots lack an exact selector and now also lack a disclosed host; both Codex slots lack an effort value the catalog requires. That is appropriate for a draft, but Findings A and B mean the executor would have to re-open decisions the draft appears to have already closed.
multi_perspective_notes.stakeholder: The artifact answers the stated question — a separate panel amendment preserving existing contracts — and refuses every adjacent authorization. The one stakeholder-facing weakness is that the single question it escalates (one SOL versus all three) is posed without the variant asymmetry that bears directly on the answer.
multi_perspective_notes.skeptic: Strongest argument against this draft is not fabrication — provenance is unusually tight, with 9/9 hashes verified — but selective rigour: the same effort dimension that received three dedicated fields on the Gemini slot received none on the two Codex slots, and host was left null in the source roster but filled in silently here. Both omissions happen to reduce the apparent size of the open decision space.

verdict_justification: FIX rather than APPROVE_DRAFT. Pre-commitment predictions targeted identity leakage, request-dropping, arithmetic error, permission creep, and result/cost promotion — all five were investigated and all five came back clean, which is a genuine strength of this artifact. The two MAJOR findings landed instead on the decision-space disclosure that the predictions did not anticipate. They are blocking for this artifact specifically because its declared function is to enumerate open choices and put one of them to the user: Finding B degrades the exact question at lines 236-241, and Finding A closes a choice the source roster had left open. Neither requires re-derivation — both are additive field corrections plus one wording amendment to line 229, and the MINOR items are one restored clause and one added translation. Remained in THOROUGH mode throughout; escalation threshold (1 CRITICAL or 3+ MAJOR) was not met. Realist Check was applied to both MAJOR findings and neither was recalibrated — each was already rated below CRITICAL on the grounds that nothing is frozen, no spend or data exists, and detection is likely at binding time; the line 228 partial mitigation for Finding B is stated explicitly rather than suppressed.
